import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 798

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/798](https://www.erdosproblems.com/798)
- [Al91] Alon, N., *Economical coverings of sets of lattice points*. Geom. Funct. Anal. (1991),
  224-230.
-/

namespace Erdos798

open Filter Asymptotics

/--
The grid $\{1,\ldots,n\}^2$, viewed as a set of points of the plane.
-/
def gridPoints (n : ℕ) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {p : ℝ × ℝ | ∃ i j : ℕ, 1 ≤ i ∧ i ≤ n ∧ 1 ≤ j ∧ j ≤ n ∧ p = ((i : ℝ), (j : ℝ))}

/--
`S` is a set of points of $\{1,\ldots,n\}^2$ such that the lines determined by the pairs of
distinct points of `S` cover all points of $\{1,\ldots,n\}^2$.
-/
def IsLineCover (n : ℕ) (S : Set (ℝ × ℝ)) : Prop :=
  S ⊆ gridPoints n ∧
    ∀ x ∈ gridPoints n, ∃ p ∈ S, ∃ q ∈ S, p ≠ q ∧ Collinear ℝ ({p, q, x} : Set (ℝ × ℝ))

/--
The minimum number of points in $\{1,\ldots,n\}^2$ such that the lines determined by these points
cover all points in $\{1,\ldots,n\}^2$.
-/
noncomputable def t (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | ∃ S : Set (ℝ × ℝ), IsLineCover n S ∧ S.ncard = k}

/--
Let $t(n)$ be the minimum number of points in $\{1,\ldots,n\}^2$ such that the $\binom{t}{2}$
lines determined by these points cover all points in $\{1,\ldots,n\}^2$.

Estimate $t(n)$. In particular, is it true that $t(n)=o(n)$?

A problem of Erdős and Purdy, who proved $t(n) \gg n^{2/3}$.

Resolved by Alon [Al91] who proved $t(n) \ll n^{2/3}\log n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos798.lean"]
theorem erdos_798 : answer(True) ↔
    (fun n : ℕ => (t n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
A problem of Erdős and Purdy, who proved $t(n) \gg n^{2/3}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_798.variants.lower_bound :
    (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (t n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Resolved by Alon [Al91] who proved $t(n) \ll n^{2/3}\log n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_798.variants.upper_bound :
    (fun n : ℕ => (t n : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ) * Real.log n) := by
  sorry

end Erdos798

reformulations.difference: Coverage by the union of pair-determined lines is expressed pointwise using two distinct selected points and `Collinear ℝ {p, q, x}`, without constructing a collection of lines.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For p ≠ q, collinearity of {p,q,x} is equivalent to x belonging to the affine line spanned by {p,q}. Existentially selecting such a pair for every grid point therefore means precisely that the union of determined lines covers the grid. Alon's definition requires at least two selected points on each determined line and does not require different pairs to determine different lines. The full predicate equivalence was proved as `Review798.lineCover_iff`.

reformulations.difference: The minimum is implemented using `sInf` and `Set.ncard`, without explicitly requiring the selected sets to be finite.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every admissible S is contained in the finite grid, so its ncard is its ordinary finite cardinality. For every n ≥ 2, the whole grid is an admissible cover, making the set of candidate cardinalities nonempty. Its natural-number infimum is attained and is the ordinary minimum. These facts and the minimum-characterization equivalence were proved in the scratch file. The exceptional totalization at n = 1 does not affect any of the three asymptotic statements.

review.notes:
All six declarations agree with the cited mathematical sources. The site records an affirmative, Lean-verified solution, consistent with `answer(True)`, the solved tags, and the formal-proof record.

Boundary checks prove `t 0 = t 1 = 0`; at n = 1 no cover exists, so zero is the empty-infimum default. This is harmless here: all theorem statements concern `atTop` on ℕ, and preservation under arbitrary changes below 2 was proved for both big-O and little-o. Independent exact determinant enumeration gives minimum cover sizes 0, nonexistent, 4, 4 for n = 0,1,2,3.

The external proof uses an integer-lattice cover definition that permits equal endpoints. Equal endpoints cover only that same point, and a cover for n ≥ 2 necessarily contains another selected point, so this does not change the relevant minimum. Its upper bound implies the main little-o claim; that analytic implication was also checked in Lean. A copy of the linked Lean 4.29.1 proof compiled under the installed 4.33.1 toolchain after three proof-only compatibility adjustments, with axioms only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.

Experiments and detailed notes are in /workspace/review/. No repository files were edited.
